title: Mouse movement
help: Sends a relative movement with Windows SendInput. Positive X moves right; positive Y moves down. Delay postpones the start. Duration 0 or one step sends the whole motion at once; multiple steps distribute the exact total ΔX/ΔY across the duration. For one action per key press, use If key down → On new press. For repeated motion while held, choose While held and Repeat until stopped. A second block with negative deltas can reverse the motion after a Wait. This does not measure or set a game's camera position. Stop with Ctrl+Alt+F7. Use macros only where permitted.

title: Recognize text
hint: Local OCR for images and PDF
help: Reads PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, WebP or PDF locally and stores the result in a variable. PDF pages are rendered in grayscale at 200 DPI and passed to Tesseract. Set PDF page to 1–100 for one page or 0 for all pages (up to 20). GIF and WebP work when the installed Tesseract build includes the matching Leptonica decoders. If the engine or language is missing, the first run offers to download the 64-bit UB Mannheim Tesseract 5.5.3 Windows build from the Tesseract GitHub release (about 24.1 MiB / 25.3 MB) and only the models named in the language field; no network request is made without explicit consent. After consent, Windows UAC asks to approve the installer; confirm the prompt to install Tesseract in LocalAppData\KLIKER Blocks\Tesseract-OCR. The app verifies the engine and continues without a restart. If UAC is declined or permission is unavailable, setup stops; you can enter the path to an existing tesseract.exe instead. Engine and file paths containing Cyrillic characters use Windows short names when available. Files are never sent over the network. Automatic setup is unavailable on 32-bit Windows. Limits: 32 MiB PDF/input, 32 MiB rendered page image, 100000 output characters and 1–120 seconds total timeout. Password-protected PDFs cannot be OCRed without a password. Example: set the PDF path to scan.pdf and PDF page to 0; Recognize text reads up to 20 pages into ocr_text, separating page results with a page break. Small or blurry text may be misread.
note: Run once and inspect the execution journal. The featured block records its actions; surrounding blocks prepare input or show the result. Choose a scanned PDF, enter a page or 0 for the first 20 pages, and install Tesseract with eng before running; the engine is not bundled.

help: Duplicates later PRINT/LOGWRITE and Message block output to a UTF-8 file in the project folder. Enter only a filename, up to 160 characters. title: Speak text
help: Speaks text with modern installed Windows voices. Text supports ${variable} and =expression, so it can read results from earlier blocks. Leave Voice blank for automatic selection by text language (ru for Cyrillic, zh for Chinese); the picker lists voice languages. Selecting a voice of the wrong language reports an error instead of silent speech. Rate is -10 to 10, volume 0–100, text at most 16000 characters. The block waits for speech to finish; stopping the scenario interrupts playback. Put it in a parallel branch for concurrent work. Voices depend on Windows; speech does not translate text.

title: Ask for text
help: Shows a text prompt and saves the answer to a variable. The default is returned if time expires before input starts; timeout 0 waits indefinitely. Cancel returns an empty string. Timeout is 0–3600 seconds, default 5. Stopping closes the dialog. Corresponds to INPUTBOX(message,default[,delay]). Set the title, X/Y and size in this block. Leave both X and Y blank to center the dialog; enter both for an exact position. Blank width or height grows to fit the text, starting at 435×205. Explicit width is 360–3000 and height 185–3000 pixels. X/Y are screen coordinates, not graph coordinates.

title: Select option
help: Shows one choice per line (1–100 choices, up to 250 characters each). Press Enter between choices in the block properties. In graph code, those line breaks appear as \n within one value line; the properties show separate choices. A template \& in properties appears as \\& in code because the code also escapes the backslash. Each line may contain a template such as =[(${counter}+2)*3]& units \&: with counter=1 it displays ‘9 units &’. OK returns the chosen 1-based index; cancel or OK without a selection returns 0. Stopping closes the dialog. Set title, X/Y and size in the block. Leave both X/Y blank to center on screen. Blank dimensions grow to fit the question and choices, starting at 465×410. Explicit width is 360–3000 and height 260–3000 pixels. X/Y are screen coordinates, not graph coordinates.
note: Run once and inspect the execution journal. The featured block records its actions; surrounding blocks prepare input or show the result. The first option displays 9 units &: [] evaluates math, & joins text, and \& prints a literal &. In properties, 11 and 22 are separate lines; graph code writes the breaks as \n.
